prompt:
Read the notice in the staff kitchen.

What happens every Friday afternoon?

All the cups and plates are washed.
The staff kitchen is closed all afternoon.
New food is put in the fridge.

Tell the team leader that she is late
Tell her customers that she is late
Call her back when the traffic is better

Show it at the staff car park

prompt:
Read the email from a customer.

Hello,

Thank you,
Ji-woo Park

choices: A refund for both chairs
Two more black chairs
A white chair instead of the black one
A black chair instead of the white one

From 8 am to 8 pm

The manager has a call at 10:00.

choices: Sign in at Reception
Find a member of staff to walk with them
Give their visitor card back
Wear their visitor card

The parcel will go back to HomeStore.
HomeStore will send a text to choose a day.
The driver will leave the parcel with a neighbour.

prompt:
Read the returns policy.

**Returns**

You can return most items within 30 days of delivery for a full refund. Items must be unused and in the original box. Sale items can be exchanged for a different item, but they cannot be refunded. Refunds are paid to the card used for the order within 5 working days.

A customer bought an item in the sale two weeks ago. It is unused, and she wants her money back. What should the agent tell her?
choices: She can get a full refund to her card.
She can exchange it, but she cannot get a refund.
She cannot return it after 14 days.
She can get a refund because it is unused.
explanation: Deciding sentence: "Sale items can be exchanged for a different item, but they cannot be refunded." Being unused does not change this rule, and the time limit is 30 days, not 14.

prompt:
Read the email from the IT team.

**Subject: Password changes**

From next Monday, all staff must change their computer password every 60 days. You will receive a reminder email 7 days before your password expires. If you do not change it in time, your account will be locked, and you will need to call the IT help desk on extension 400.

What happens if a staff member does not change their password in time?
choices: They receive a second reminder email.
The IT help desk changes it for them.
Their account is locked.
They must change it every 7 days.

prompt:

choices: Ask the customer for a photo of her receipt
Wait until Leila is back at work
Close the ticket in the system
Check the payment with the finance team

prompt:
Read the notice.

Why should staff sign up early?
choices: Each session has a limited number of places.
The sessions last three hours.
The team sheet will be removed on 14 March.
Staff must attend both of the training sessions.
explanation: Deciding sentence: "There are only 12 places in each session, so please sign up early." The length of a session is not the reason, the sign-up date is 10 March, and staff "only need to attend one".

prompt:
Read the email from a customer.

Dear Customer Care,

I called on Monday about my broken washing machine. The agent, Joseph, was very helpful and booked a repair for Thursday. However, nobody came on Thursday, and nobody called me. I have now taken two days off work. Please call me today to book a new date.

Regards,
Anil Mehta

Why is Mr Mehta writing?
choices: The agent he spoke to was not helpful.
The repair person did not come on Thursday.
His machine broke again after the repair.
He wants to cancel the repair visit completely.

prompt:
Read the company policy.

**Identity checks on calls**

Before you discuss any account, ask the caller for their full name, date of birth and the first line of their address. If any of these details do not match our records, do not give any account information. You may still give general information, such as our opening hours or prices.

A caller gives the wrong date of birth. What can the agent still do?
choices: Tell the caller their account balance
Change the address on the account
Tell the caller the opening hours
Read out the caller's last payment
explanation: Deciding sentence: "You may still give general information, such as our opening hours or prices." The balance, the address and the last payment are account information, which must not be given when a detail does not match.

prompt:
Read the message from a supervisor.

**Supervisor:** Quick reminder for everyone: customers are waiting more than 6 minutes today. Please keep your after-call notes short and finish them within 1 minute. Take your breaks only at your planned times. If you need to leave your desk for something urgent, send me a message first.

What should an agent do before leaving the desk for something urgent?
choices: Finish all their after-call notes
Wait for their planned break time
Ask the caller to wait 6 minutes
Send the supervisor a message
explanation: Deciding sentence: "If you need to leave your desk for something urgent, send me a message first." Notes and planned breaks are separate reminders, and 6 minutes is today's waiting time for customers.

prompt:

Stay in the building
Call Reception to check
Wait one minute, then leave

Pay a cancellation fee

To the office manager

The department manager

prompt:
Read the company policy.

**Damaged items**

If an item arrives damaged, the customer should send us a photo within 7 days of delivery. Agents may then offer a replacement or a full refund, whichever the customer prefers. If the photo is sent after 7 days, agents may only offer a replacement, unless the damage could not have been seen when the item was unpacked, for example an electrical fault. In that case, treat it as if it had been reported in time.

A customer reports an electrical fault 10 days after delivery. The fault only appeared when the item was first used. What can the agent offer?
choices: A replacement only
A replacement or a full refund
A full refund only
Nothing, because 7 days have passed
explanation: Deciding sentences: "...unless the damage could not have been seen when the item was unpacked, for example an electrical fault. In that case, treat it as if it had been reported in time." Reported in time means "a replacement or a full refund". "A replacement only" is the rule for other late reports.

prompt:

The task will go automatically to the next free agent at the agreed time. Why must notes be more complete from 1 October?
choices: Customers will be able to read the notes.
Managers will check the shared calendar.
Another agent may make the callback.
Callbacks must be made within one hour.
explanation: Deciding sentence: "This means the agent who took the first call may not be the one who calls back, so your notes must be complete enough for a colleague to continue." Customers reading notes and a one-hour limit are not mentioned, and the shared calendar will no longer be used.

Write down any changes that customers ask for, and enter them after 06:00. Card payments can still be taken by phone, as they use a separate system.

A customer calls at 03:00 on Sunday to change their address. What should the agent do?

Ask the customer to change it in the app
Ask the customer to call back on Monday
Write the request down and enter it after 06:00

prompt:
Read the chat message from a customer.

**Customer:** I've been charged a 15 dollar late fee, but I paid on the 28th, which is before the due date on my bill. My bank says the money left my account that same day. I don't mind paying fees when I've made a mistake, but that clearly isn't the case here.

What is the customer's main point?
choices: The fee is unfair because the payment was on time.
The bank made a mistake with the payment.
Customers should never have to pay late fees.
The due date printed on the bill is wrong.
explanation: Deciding sentences: "I paid on the 28th, which is before the due date on my bill" and "I don't mind paying fees when I've made a mistake, but that clearly isn't the case here." The bank confirms the payment, the customer accepts fees in general, and does not say the due date is wrong.

prompt:
Read the guide for agents.

**Escalation guide**

Transfer a call to a team leader only if: the customer has asked for a manager twice after you have tried to help; the customer mentions legal action; or the solution needs a refund above your limit. Do not transfer a call just because a customer is angry. In most cases, a calm explanation and a clear next step solve the problem faster than a transfer.

According to the guide, which call should be transferred to a team leader?
choices: A customer is shouting about a late delivery.
A customer says they will take the company to court.
A customer asks for a manager for the first time.
A customer wants a refund that is within your limit.
explanation: Deciding text: transfer if "the customer mentions legal action". Taking the company to court is legal action. "Do not transfer a call just because a customer is angry", one request is not "twice", and a refund within your limit does not need a team leader.

It will be checked in a monthly test instead.

prompt:
Read the company policy.

**Call recording**

All calls are recorded for training and quality. If a customer asks for the recording to be stopped, explain that it cannot be stopped during the call, but that they can ask in writing for it to be deleted after 30 days. Card numbers must never be said aloud on a recorded line: transfer the customer to the automated payment line instead.

A customer wants to pay by card during the call. What should the agent do?
choices: Stop the recording before taking the number
Transfer the customer to the automated line
Ask the customer to read the number slowly
Ask the customer to send the number in writing
explanation: Deciding sentence: "Card numbers must never be said aloud on a recorded line: transfer the customer to the automated payment line instead." The recording "cannot be stopped during the call", reading the number aloud is not allowed, and writing is only for asking to delete a recording.

However, you put her on hold four times without telling her why, and she sounded more and more annoyed. Next time, tell the customer what you are checking and roughly how long it will take.

What does the supervisor want the agent to improve?
choices: Giving customers correct information
Being more polite to customers
Explaining to customers why they are on hold
Finishing calls more quickly
explanation: Deciding sentence: "Next time, tell the customer what you are checking and roughly how long it will take." The supervisor praises the agent for being polite and correct, and does not mention call length.

prompt:
Read the email from a manager.

**Subject: Response times**

Some of you have asked whether the new target of answering emails within 4 hours means that quality matters less. It does not. A quick reply that fails to solve the problem simply produces a second email, which is counted against the original target anyway. If an email genuinely needs more investigation, send a short holding reply within 4 hours explaining what you are doing, and follow up with a full answer once you have it.

According to the writer, why does a fast but unhelpful reply not help with the target?
choices: Managers will check the quality of every reply.
Customers would rather wait for a complete answer.
Holding replies are not allowed under the new target.
It leads to another email that still counts against the target.
explanation: Deciding sentence: "A quick reply that fails to solve the problem simply produces a second email, which is counted against the original target anyway." Manager checks and customer preferences are not mentioned, and the writer recommends holding replies.

prompt:
Read the company policy.

**Goodwill credits**

Agents may offer a goodwill credit where the company has clearly made an error, even if the customer has not asked for one. Credits should not, however, be used simply to end a difficult call where no error has occurred, as this creates the expectation that complaining will be rewarded. Where it is unclear whether the company is at fault, agents should log the case for review rather than make a decision during the call.

A customer is angry about a delay, but it is not yet clear whose fault it was. What should the agent do?
choices: Log the case so that it can be reviewed
Offer a small credit to calm the customer
Tell the customer no credit is possible
Offer a credit only if the customer asks
explanation: Deciding sentence: "Where it is unclear whether the company is at fault, agents should log the case for review rather than make a decision during the call." A credit to calm the call is what the policy warns against, refusing any credit is a decision the agent should not make yet, and whether the customer asks is not the test.
